prompt: What is the difference between == and .equals() for object references?
choices: == is faster; equals() is more accurate
== checks if two references point to the same object; .equals() checks logical equality
== checks value equality; .equals() checks reference equality
They behave identically for all types
explanation: String a = new String("hi"); String b = new String("hi"); a == b is false (different objects). a.equals(b) is true (same content). For primitives, == compares values directly.
